newsitem.title: USA: Nearby CME live cattle close at day's high.
newsitem.headline: Nearby CME live cattle close at day's high.

text.p: October CME live cattle futures remained strong at the close and posted the day's high in the closing range while other months ended unchanged to lower. Feeders ended mostly lower.

Continued rolling of short positions into back months and fundamental support from expected firm fed cattle prices this week boosted October live cattle to its high in the closing range, traders said.
Packers are expected to pay $72 to $73 per cwt for fed cattle as they are short bought. Feedlot pricing stances are holding firm on the reduced fed cattle supply, they said.

December fell for a fairly large loss after midsession as the position rolling and technical pressure touched off sell stops. But local short covering and buying by RBH pared the loss in late trade, they added.
E.D.& F. Man, RBH, Merrill Lynch and R.J. O'Brien were notable buyers of October late, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, Term Commodities actively bought October 72 puts and sold 71 puts on a two-for-one basis, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures remained lightly traded and values eased late following deferred live cattle. Higher corn futures also weighed on prices after lending support early, traders said.
R.J. O'Brien and Merrill Lynch sold late and Refco sold at the close, traders said. Stone Traders and Lind-Waldock sold early, pit sources said.
The latest CME feeder cattle index was off $0.16 at $63.74 per cwt.
Live cattle closed 0.450 cent higher to 0.125 lower with only October up at 73.175 cents. Feeder cattle ended 0.050 cent higher to 0.250 lower with October off 0.050 at 63.550.
